simple.meaning: יָגֵעַ (yâgêaʻ) is a Hebrew word meaning “tired ; hence (transitive) tiresome.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: יָגֵעַ (H3023) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Deuteronomy 25:18, with occurrences in Deuteronomy, 2 Samuel, Ecclesiastes.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יָגֵעַ (H3023) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in יָגֵעַ (H3023) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: יָגֵעַ (yâgêaʻ) / H3023 is traced through Deuteronomy 25:18, 2 Samuel 17:2, Ecclesiastes 1:8 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: how he met you by the way, and struck the rearmost of you, all who were feeble behind you, when you were faint and weary; and he didn’t fear God.

timeline.evidenceText: how he met you by the way, and struck the rearmost of you, all who were feeble behind you, when you were faint and weary; and he didn’t fear God.
I will come on him while he is weary and exhausted, and will make him afraid. All the people who are with him will flee. I will strike the king only,
All things are full of weariness beyond uttering. The eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.
